newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil to develop new N. Sea gas fields.
newsitem.headline: Statoil to develop new N. Sea gas fields.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday the Oil Ministry had included phase II of the North Sea Gullfaks satellites among the allocations to supply gas to continental Europe from 1999.

The ministry also has selected the development of the Huldra find in the same area, which will start deliveries in 2000, when Heidrun and Norne in the Norwegian Sea also will begin supplying associated gas.
Statoil said that the allocation of these fields to Norwegian gas sales contracts meant that development of the prospects could begin immediately.

The Status Weekly newsletter said Statoil would be able to plan a pipeline 37 km and 121 km in length to run from Heidrun and Norne respectively to tie into the export riser base on the Aasgard field in the Haltenbanken off mid-Norway.
The link will allow gas from the two fields to flow to the Kaarstoe terminal, north of Stavanger. Heidrun already pipes gas to Tjeldbergodden in mid-Norway.
Statoil said the Troll and Sleipner fields can supply gas for additional supply contracts from 1999, but it remained uncertain how much extra gas would be required in 1999-2000.
The ministry plans further gas contract allocations next year, it said.
